title: Family, Discounts and Emotions Drive Gen Z Festive Overspending Across India
excerpt: A YouGov and Rukam Capital study of 4,002 Indians aged 18-29 finds six in ten spend more at festivals, family accounts for 74% of gifting, and AI now helps one in four choose gifts — while research, not creators, closes the sale.
body:
• A YouGov and Rukam Capital study of 4,002 Gen Z respondents aged 18-29 found six in ten spend more during festivals, with family expectations the biggest driver of overspending.
  • Parents and family account for 74% of festive gifting, far ahead of friends and partners; self-gifting accounts for 30%.
  • Online search is the top source of festive inspiration at 41%, and one in four respondents already uses AI for gift ideas.
  • For shoppers: nearly six in ten use AI at least occasionally to compare prices, but only 6% buy straight after a creator recommendation and 46% research more first — quality (51%) and price (49%) still decide the purchase.

Family expectations, discounts and emotion are driving India's youngest shoppers to spend beyond their plans this festive season, according to a YouGov report produced with Rukam Capital and covered by Mint. The study surveyed 4,002 Gen Z respondents aged 18 to 29 and found that festive shopping varies by region and state, shaped by family expectations, personal preferences and digital discovery.

Six in ten respondents said they spend more during festivals. The spending is a mix of planning and spontaneity rather than pure impulse: nearly a third of Gen Z consumers said their festive spending is planned in advance, according to The Hindu BusinessLine, which reported the same Rukam Capital and YouGov findings.

Family first, then the self

Family remains the emotional anchor of the season. Parents and family dominate gifting at 74%, far ahead of friends and partners, and the report identifies family expectations as the biggest driver of overspending. Festive budgets, in other words, are stretched less by personal indulgence than by obligations at home — gifts for parents and relatives that shoppers are reluctant to cut.

Self-expression is reshaping that tradition rather than replacing it. Self-gifting accounts for 30% of festive purchases, and 50% of respondents opt for healthier snacking during the season, a sign that celebration and personal wellbeing now sit in the same basket. The full study findings, summarised by FM Live, describe the pattern as tradition meeting tech and self-expression.

Research before the register

Discovery has moved online, but discovery rarely closes the sale. Online search leads festive inspiration at 41%, while social media and creators account for 29%. Only 6% of respondents buy a product straight after a creator recommendation, and 46% said they research more before making a purchase. Gen Z trusts its own research most, at 27%, ahead of friends at 20% and online reviews at 15%. Concerns about fake or deepfake content push 32% to verify sellers, and 29% prefer established brands they trust.

AI has entered that research process. Nearly six in ten respondents use AI at least occasionally for product research, mainly to compare options and find the best price, and one in four already uses AI for gift ideas. The trust has limits: 70% are comfortable with AI recommending products and services, but only 49% would allow AI to decide without their approval. Around 30% also call out influencer overuse, forced slang or trend-chasing by brands.

Convenience competes with that caution. Quick-commerce adoption stands at 28%, and one in five respondents admit they have become more impulsive shoppers. Even so, quality at 51% and price at 49% remain the top purchase drivers, well ahead of reviews or trends.

What the report signals

Archana Jahagirdar, founder and managing partner of Rukam Capital, said India's next growth story is being shaped by Gen Z and that the brands that win will be those that earn trust, not just attention. The numbers support that reading for retailers and consumer brands selling into the festive season: the overspend is real, but it is directed — toward family first, toward researched purchases, and toward sellers who can survive a price comparison and a credibility check. For households, the practical lesson is the mirror image: the budget pressure point is gifting for family, so that is where a festive budget needs its clearest limit before the season starts.
